∀ {d q : ℕ} (hq : 2 * q + 1 < d),
  let D := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q + 1))
  let Ω := Fin (q + 1) → D
  let μ : Measure Ω := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin (q + 1) => stdGaussian D)
  let M := Matrix (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) (Fin (q + 1) × Fin (q + 1)) ℝ
  let r : ℝ := ((q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
  let L : ℝ := 2 * r + 3 * Real.log (1000 * (d : ℝ))
  let α : Fin d → ℝ := fun i => ((i.val : ℝ) + 1 - 1 / 2) * Real.pi / (d : ℝ)
  let tvec : Fin d → Fin (q + 1) → ℝ := fun i k =>
    if k.val = 0 then 1 else Real.sqrt 2 * Real.cos ((k.val : ℝ) * α i)
  let row : Fin d → Ω → E := fun i ω =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun b : Fin (q + 1) => ω b i)
  let Y : Fin d → Ω → M := fun i ω =>
    if ‖row i ω‖ ^ 2 ≤ L then
      (d : ℝ)⁻¹ • Matrix.kronecker
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)) (WithLp.ofLp (row i ω)))
        (Matrix.vecMulVec (tvec i) (tvec i))
    else 0
  let mean : Fin d → M := fun i => ∫ ω, Y i ω ∂μ
  let Z : Fin d → Ω → M := fun i ω => Y i ω - mean i
  let w : Bool → Fin d → ℝ := fun useCos i =>
    if useCos = true then Real.cos (((2 * q + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * α i) else 1
  let sign : Bool → ℝ := fun minus => if minus = true then -1 else 1
  let S : Bool → Bool → Ω → M := fun useCos minus ω =>
    sign minus • ∑ i : Fin d, w useCos i • Z i ω
  let Rstar : ℝ := 2 * r * (L + 1) / (d : ℝ)
  ∀ s : ℝ, ∀ useCos minus : Bool,
    let G : Ω → M := fun ω => NormedSpace.exp (s • S useCos minus ω)
    let MX : M := ∫ ω, G ω ∂μ
    let B : ℝ := r ^ 2 * Real.exp (|s| * ((d : ℝ) * Rstar))
    Integrable G μ ∧ MX.PosDef ∧
      Matrix.trace MX = (∫ ω, Matrix.trace (G ω) ∂μ) ∧
      0 < Matrix.trace MX ∧ Matrix.trace MX ≤ B

Measure Ω is a measure on the given measurable space. IsProbabilityMeasure means total mass one. Integrable f μ is Bochner integrability of the displayed matrix-valued function, and ∫ω,f ω∂μ is its Bochner integral under precisely μ.

Let d,q ∈ ℕ satisfy 2q + 1 < d. Put n = q + 1 and r = n, with r regarded as a real number. Let D = ℝ^d and E = ℝ^n with their Euclidean structures, let Ω = (Fin n → D), and let μ = ⨂_{b∈Fin n} γ_D, where γ_D is the centered standard Gaussian law on D. Let M be the real square-matrix algebra indexed, in each direction, by Fin n × Fin n; thus its matrices have size n² × n².

For i ∈ Fin d and k ∈ Fin n define
  L = 2r + 3 log(1000d),
  α_i = ((i + 1 - 1/2)π)/d,
  t_i(k) = 1 if k = 0, and t_i(k) = √2 cos(k α_i) otherwise.
All natural-number entries in these real formulas are cast to ℝ, and i and k denote the zero-based integer values of their Fin indices. For ω ∈ Ω let x_i(ω) ∈ E have coordinate x_i(ω)_b = ω(b)_i. Define
  Y_i(ω) = d⁻¹ [(x_i(ω)x_i(ω)ᵀ) ⊗ (t_i t_iᵀ)] if ‖x_i(ω)‖² ≤ L,
  Y_i(ω) = 0 otherwise,
  m_i = ∫_Ω Y_i(ω) dμ(ω),
  Z_i(ω) = Y_i(ω) - m_i.
Here ⊗ is the Kronecker product with the x-factor first and the t-factor second. The truncation includes equality at L, and the other branch is the zero matrix.

For Boolean values c,e define
  w_c(i) = cos((2q + 1)α_i) if c = true, and w_c(i) = 1 if c = false,
  σ_e = -1 if e = true, and σ_e = 1 if e = false,
  S_{c,e}(ω) = σ_e ∑_{i∈Fin d} w_c(i) Z_i(ω),
  R_* = 2r(L + 1)/d.
For every real s and every pair of Boolean values c,e, set
  G(ω) = exp_M(s S_{c,e}(ω)),
  MX = ∫_Ω G(ω) dμ(ω),
  B = r² exp_ℝ(|s| d R_*).
Then G is Bochner integrable with respect to μ; MX is positive definite; tr(MX) = ∫_Ω tr(G(ω)) dμ(ω); and 0 < tr(MX) ≤ B. The exponential exp_M is the power-series exponential of the matrix algebra, exp_ℝ is the scalar exponential, and tr is the ordinary unnormalized trace. Positive definite means symmetric with a strictly positive quadratic form on every nonzero vector.

/-! Positive definiteness of the true probability mean. This author-derived
canonical background reuses the existing PSD integral node and proves strict
positivity separately for every nonzero quadratic-form test vector. Generic
integrability and AE-PD data must be derived internally by source consumers.
Empty finite matrix indices are allowed. -/

open MeasureTheory
open scoped Matrix.Norms.L2Operator
noncomputable section
universe u v
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.RealMatrixPositiveDefIntegral

theorem integral_posDef :
∀ {ι : Type u} {Ω : Type v} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ],
  ∀ (f : Ω → Matrix ι ι ℝ), Integrable f μ →
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, (f ω).PosDef) → (∫ ω, f ω ∂μ).PosDef
 := by
  classical
  intro ι Ω _ _ _ μ _ f hf hpos
  have hpsd :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.RealMatrixPositiveIntegral.integral_posSemidef
      f hf (hpos.mono fun _ h => h.posSemidef)
  apply Matrix.PosDef.of_dotProduct_mulVec_pos hpsd.isHermitian
  intro x hx
  let L : Matrix ι ι ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ :=
    { toFun := fun A => dotProduct (star x) (A.mulVec x)
      map_add' := by intro A B; simp [Matrix.add_mulVec, dotProduct_add]
      map_smul' := by intro c A; simp [Matrix.smul_mulVec, dotProduct_smul] }
  let φ : Matrix ι ι ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ := L.toContinuousLinearMap
  have hfi : Integrable (fun ω => φ (f ω)) μ := φ.integrable_comp hf
  have hstrict : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, 0 < φ (f ω) := by
    filter_upwards [hpos] with ω hω
    exact hω.dotProduct_mulVec_pos hx
  have hnonneg : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, 0 ≤ φ (f ω) := hstrict.mono fun _ h => h.le
  have hintpos : 0 < ∫ ω, φ (f ω) ∂μ := by
    have hne : (∫ ω, φ (f ω) ∂μ) ≠ 0 := by
      intro hz
      have hzAE := (integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg_ae hnonneg hfi).mp hz
      obtain ⟨ω, hωpos, hωzero⟩ := (hstrict.and hzAE).exists
      exact (ne_of_gt hωpos) hωzero
    exact lt_of_le_of_ne (integral_nonneg_of_ae hnonneg) (Ne.symm hne)
  rw [φ.integral_comp_comm hf] at hintpos
  exact hintpos

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.RealMatrixPositiveDefIntegral

lesson.title: Positive definiteness of the true probability mean
lesson.statement: The Bochner mean of an integrable finite real matrix field that is positive definite almost everywhere is positive definite.
lesson.formula: f\in L^1(\mu;\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathcal I}(\mathbb R)),\quad f(\omega)\succ0\ \mu\text{-a.e.}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\int f\,d\mu\succ0.
assumptions: Let \(\mathcal I\) be any finite index type, including the empty type, and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure on an arbitrary measurable space. Let \(f:\Omega\to\operatorname{Mat}_{\mathcal I}(\mathbb R)\) be Bochner integrable and positive definite \(\mu\)-almost everywhere.

Positive definite means Hermitian with strictly positive quadratic form on every nonzero vector. The mean is the actual matrix-valued Bochner integral under the displayed law. No common positive spectral lower bound is assumed. For an empty index type, the nonzero-vector condition is vacuous.

For the associated private consumer, \(d,q\in\mathbb N\), \(2q+1<d\), \(r=q+1\), \(\Omega=(\mathbb R^d)^r\), and \(\mu=\gamma_d^{\otimes r}\). This is the original unconditional product Gaussian law; \(q=0\) is included.

For physical rows \(i=1,\ldots,d\), let \(\alpha_i=(i-\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(t_i=(1,\sqrt2\cos\alpha_i,\ldots,\sqrt2\cos(q\alpha_i))\), \(\Phi_i=(\omega_b(i))_{b=0}^q\), and \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\). Lean explicitly converts zero-based \(i\) using \(i.val+1\).

Let \(Y_i=d^{-1}(\Phi_i\Phi_i^\top\otimes t_it_i^\top)\mathbf1_{\{\|\Phi_i\|^2\le L\}}\), \(m_i=\int Y_i\,d\mu\), and \(Z_i=Y_i-m_i\). The cutoff includes equality and uses the same physical row; the Gaussian factor comes first in the paired matrix index, of size \(r^2\).

Choose \(w_i=1\) or \(w_i=\cos((2q+1)\alpha_i)\), and one global \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}\). Define \(S=\varepsilon\sum_iw_i Z_i\), \(R_*=2r(L+1)/d\), \(G_s(\omega)=e^{sS(\omega)}\), \(M_s=\int G_s\,d\mu\), and \(B_s=r^2e^{|s|dR_*}\). For every real \(s\), the Gaussian application gives \(G_s\in L^1(\mu)\), \(M_s\succ0\), \(\operatorname{tr}M_s=\int\operatorname{tr}G_s\,d\mu\), and \(0<\operatorname{tr}M_s\le B_s\).

All Gaussian probability structure, measurability, Hermiticity, radius bounds, exponential norm bounds, integrability and positive definiteness needed here are obtained internally or through existing canonical source producers. They follow from the definitions and the proved bounds. The trace is ordinary and unnormalized; the exponential is matrix-algebra power-series exponential. The signs do not assert equality of signed laws or MGFs.

steps.text: For the same Hermitian S(ω), continuous functional calculus identifies exp(sx) with the matrix-algebra exponential exp(sS(ω)). Continuity of the matrix exponential and measurability of S give matrix measurability; the uniform bound under the probability law gives matrix Bochner integrability. steps.title: Commute ordinary trace with the mean and retain the exact cap
steps.text: Ordinary trace is a continuous linear map on this finite real matrix space, so it commutes with the integrable matrix mean and yields scalar trace integrability.
